name: AresDB
tagline: Uber's GPU-accelerated real-time analytics store; open-sourced in 2018 and inactive since 2020.
description: AresDB is a real-time analytics engine Uber built to power internal dashboards such as its Summary Dashboard, and open-sourced in November 2018. It keeps columnar data mostly in host memory (an uncompressed live store for fresh upserts and a sorted, run-length-compressed archive store partitioned by day, backed by redo logs on disk) and ships filtered batches to NVIDIA GPUs for aggregation, fact-to-dimension hash joins, HyperLogLog counts and geo intersection. Ingestion is via HTTP upsert batches, typically fed from Kafka, Flink or Spark, with primary-key deduplication and late-arriving backfill. Queries use AQL, a structured JSON/YAML format rather than SQL. Uber stopped developing it in public after April 2020, so it is a reference design rather than a deployable product.
statusNote: No commits since April 2020 and no release beyond v0.0.2; Uber has not maintained the open-source project. Apache Pinot, Druid or ClickHouse cover the use case.

pricing.notes: Requires NVIDIA GPUs and the CUDA toolkit (under NVIDIA's own EULA).

scale.notes: Data must fit a host memory budget, with archive batches loaded on demand; the open-source release was effectively single-instance.

strengths: GPU execution gives sub-second aggregations over large fact tables
Upserts with primary-key deduplication and late-data backfill
Built-in fact/dimension joins, HyperLogLog distinct counts and geo intersection
Battle-tested design notes published by Uber engineering
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2020; early versioning (v0.0.x) and no community
Needs NVIDIA GPUs with a specific CUDA toolchain
Custom AQL query format instead of SQL
Strings limited to enum encodings with equality-only filtering
useCases: Reference architecture for dashboard backends with upserts
notIdealFor: Teams without GPU infrastructure or Go/CUDA expertise
